chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, a man may drink a single draught and Allah will cause him to enter Paradise. I asked: How is that? He said: Indeed, a man drinks water, then stops drinking, sets the vessel aside while still desiring it, and praises Allah. Then he returns and drinks again, sets it aside while still desiring it, and praises Allah. Then he returns and drinks again, and Allah, Exalted and Glorious, obligates Paradise for him because of that.
ai.seo_question: How does pausing while drinking water lead to entering Paradise?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the concept of *al-shukr* (gratitude) through the specific act of restraining one's desire (*al-imsak*) even when still craving the object, thereby transforming a mundane physical act into an act of worship. The Imam emphasizes that the spiritual merit lies not in the deprivation itself, but in the conscious intention and praise of Allah while the desire remains active, illustrating the Shia emphasis on inner states (*batin*) accompanying outward actions. This practice serves as a microcosm of self-discipline, where the believer masters their *nafs* (ego) to earn divine reward.

en.basel-kadem: 16.	We were told by my father, may Allah granrt him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Muhammed bin Isa, from Abbas bin Ma’ruf, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Muhammed bin Huss’ain, from Muhammed bin Fudail, from al-‘Azrami, that he said: I was with Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, in the home (of his), sitting under the drain, while one man was quarreling with another man, and one of them was saying to his companion: By Allah, do you not know where the wind runs from? When he had said that much to him, Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said to him: And do you know from where the winds runs? He said: No, but I hear the people say. I then said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: From where does the wind run, may I be sacrificed for you?

He said: Indeed, the wind is constrained under this Levantine pillar, and when Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, wants to send off some of it, He makes it come out: if it is (to be towards the) south, it is south; if it is (to be towards the) north, it is north; if it is (to be) cast fiercely, it is cast fiercely; and if it is (to be) mild, it is mild. He then said: The sign of that is that you still see this pillar moving during winter and summer, continuously, at the night along with the day.
